newsitem.title: KENYA: Hundreds of demonstrators rally in Nairobi park.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds of demonstrators rally in Nairobi park.

text.p: Several hundred supporters of a one-day general strike in Kenya called by opposition groups demonstrated in a Nairobi park on Friday but police did not intervene.
Several youths were chased and beaten by demonstrators, apparently because they were suspected of being ruling party members or plainclothes police, but overall the rally started in relative calm.

There was no sign of riot police or members of the paramilitary General Service Unit (GSU) as leaders of an opposition-backed alliance demanding constitutional reforms from President Daniel arap Moi's government addressed their supporters in Uhuru park.
"Moi must go, Moi must go," chanted groups of youths heading for the rally. But in contrast to rallies in the capital in June and July there was no immediate stone-throwing or clashes with police.
Most shops in Nairobi closed on Friday because their owners feared violence and looting during the one-day general strike.

But many workers, perhaps fearing penalties after the government declared the strike unlawful, ignored the protest to back demands for pre-election political reforms from Moi, 73 and in power for 19 years.
